findings.claim: Unrelated change to the serializer runtime: the `case <= byte.MaxValue` branch (TryWriteUInt8) is removed from the unsigned-integer writer. Values 128..255 would now be written as UInt16 (0xcd) instead of UInt8 (0xcc). This changes the wire format, wastes bytes, and is out of scope for a generator/analyzer crash fix; it is also likely to break byte-exact tests.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint/ulong values such as 128, 200 and 255 with base-built and head-built MessagePack and compare bytes. Base emits 0xcc 0xNN; head emits 0xcd 0x00 0xNN. Also run the MessagePackWriter/primitives unit tests.

findings.claim: Adding README and MsgPack004 docs says that diagnostics for referenced-assembly types are reported by the defining assembly. This matches the deliberate behaviour recorded in [L12], so it is fine. The new docs are an acknowledged fit, not a defect.

receipt_plan.detail: [L12] Types from referenced assemblies are deliberately not analysed; the defining assembly owns diagnostics, so the documented behaviour is consistent.

findings.claim: The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper drops every diagnostic whose location is not in a syntax tree of the current compilation, for all diagnostics routed through reportDiagnostic. This includes diagnostics created with a null location (e.g. MemberNeedsKey from FirstOrDefault()), and any diagnostic for source-less cases in the current compilation, which will now be silently suppressed. It is a broad behaviour change beyond the three crash sites. It is consistent with [L12] for metadata types, but could hide legitimate diagnostics, such as ones with Location.None for in-compilation symbols.

receipt_plan.detail: Add analyzer tests for diagnostics that previously reported with Location.None or additional locations (e.g. MsgPack004 on a property without a declaring syntax reference in the same compilation) and confirm they are still reported. Run the full analyzer test suite for regressions.
